title: The Two Years Between Oxford Nanopore's Promise and Its First Users
conflicts: Cause of the 2012-14 delay: Lara Marks's history and GEN give a microchip design flaw, Phys.org (2014) said trouble scaling the pore technology and finding alternative materials; story uses the chip flaw, attributed. Participants: ~3,000 applications (Sanghera; Marks), ~500 accepted by June 2014 (Marks), over 1,000 labs over the programme (F1000Research); story gives applications and first acceptances only. MAP start: April 2014 in written sources vs Sanghera's '2015' in a podcast; April 2014 used. Commercial availability: by July 2015 (IP Group) vs May 2015 (Wikipedia); story says by July 2015.
notes: The one talQen mention for this group (reflection). Company field written as 'Oxford Nanopore' because the repeat screen matched 'Technologies' in the unrelated Tiny Speck/Slack Technologies edition; noted in research_notes. Sanghera's podcast remarks are paraphrased because the transcript is speech-recognition; 'customer-ready' is quoted from the 2012 press release. Nature news pieces were not usable (preview only).
